brief:
Today, 19 November, is Push B. Nothing new has been logged since Legs A on 17 November, and 18 November was the rest day, so tonight's numbers are yesterday's, unchanged, and most of the review below repeats yesterday's.

What changed is the neck. You wrote on 18 November that there were no neck exercises in the program and that this is an obvious miss. You were right: neck was not even one of the muscles the program counted. Since this morning (version 15) it has its own weekly range and two lifts that need only a flat bench and a plate, since you have no harness and no neck machine. Lying plate neck flexion: on your back, head off the end of the bench, towel and plate on your forehead, chin to chest. It goes last on Push A, two sets of 15 to 20, first on 22 November. Lying plate neck extension: face down, head off the end, towel and plate on the back of your head, lift your head until you face forward. It goes straight after the shrugs on Pull B, two sets of 15 to 20, first tomorrow, 20 November. Both start with a 10 lb plate for 15 on each set, and move up only when both sets reach 20 with no neck pain the next day. That is 4 sets a week to start, because there is no neck training anywhere in your log; it grows toward 8 once both have run twice cleanly. Push A becomes 19 sets and Pull B 22.

Push B tonight: shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four. Chest press 165 for 10 on all three, one weight; this is the heavier chest press day (8 to 10 reps), and Push A uses the same machine for 10 to 12, which is why the two cards show different numbers. Lateral raise 17.5 for 13, 13, 13, then 12 on the fourth set. High-to-low crossover 30.5 for 15, 13. Reverse pec deck 97.5 for 13 on all three. Rope pushdown 50.5 for 12 on all three. Overhead dumbbell triceps extension, one dumbbell in both hands behind your head: 60 for 12, 12.

A correction: yesterday I asked whether your gym has a standing or seated calf machine. Your 23 July photos of the whole gym already answered that, and I should have read them first. There is neither; calf raises are done on the leg press. The question I do have is different: calves get 9 counted sets a week (6 of them direct calf press sets), near the bottom of their 8 to 16 range, and the stage scores them. More calf work at your gym means a second calf lift: a standing calf raise on the smith machine, or a single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step. That would take a leg day past the three calf sets you settled in July and August. Do you want that? Until you say, calves stay at three a day.

Show prep, 14 weeks out: the plan is under this brief, unchanged from yesterday. Prep starts 9 December after the lighter week (from 25 November) and assessment week (from 2 December). Still missing: a bodyweight (none logged since 23 August), your division, photos or a waist measurement, and whether someone else sets your diet. The bodyweight is the urgent one; the Bodyweight button is on the workout screen.

Still open: if the shrug's fourth set is missing again tomorrow on Pull B, that card drops to three sets. Side delts are still behind rear delts on the counted number (10 against 12.5); the 24 November review decides the next step after tonight's and 22 November's four-set lateral nights. One more open item: your gym file says the cables move in 5 lb steps with 1.25 lb add-ons, but your logs show 1.5 lb steps (49 to 50.5); until that is sorted out, on the cable lifts set the nearest weight the stack gives and log what it reads.

block.why: Nothing new has been logged since the last review: the latest night in the repo is still Legs A on 17 November, and 18 November was set as a rest day after nine sessions in a row. So every load and every verdict that rests on the log repeats yesterday's, and the Push B card is the one written yesterday, unchanged. Two things did change, and neither comes from the log. First, you wrote in chat on 18 November that the program had no neck exercises. Neck was not in the muscles the program counted; since then it is, and today it gets a range (4 to 12 counted sets a week) and two lifts built for your gym: lying plate neck flexion on Push A and lying plate neck extension on Pull B, two sets each of 15 to 20. Push A goes from 17 to 19 sets and Pull B from 20 to 22; the week goes from 119 to 123. Second, the gym file now carries your 23 July photos of the whole gym, and they answer yesterday's question about a calf machine: there is none, so that question is withdrawn. It is still week 4 of 4 of the build block restarted at the New York gym on 28 October. The build runs to 24 November, the lighter week is 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 102 days away. The block is doing what a build block should: every lift logged at this gym since 9 November went up or held its weight. The days run Push B 19 November, Pull B 20, Legs B 21, Push A 22, Pull A 23, rest 24 November. Adding two new lifts in the last build week is deliberate: they each run once before the lighter week, which gives the December assessment a starting weight for both. The side-delt decision stays dated to the 24 November review, after the four-set lateral nights on 19 and 22 November.

chest.why: Eighteen sets a week, inside the new 12 to 20 range; seven of them are aimed at the upper chest (smith incline 4, low-to-high crossover 3). No chest work since 15 November, so the lifts repeat: chest press 157.5 for 12, 12, 12 and smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8 on 15 November, low-to-high crossover 12.5 for 15 on all three. All going up at the New York gym. Sets hold; the weights move. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 18 are direct sets; 12.5 a week done on average over the last four weeks (the fourth is this week, which so far holds only Pull A on 16 November and Legs A on 17 November).

front-delts.why: Fifteen counted, inside 6 to 16. Eight are the two presses that lead each push day (smith incline 4, shoulder press 4); the other seven are half credit from the chest press, crossovers and dips. No set is in the week only for front delts, so the only way to lower this is to cut chest or shoulder pressing, and neither should be cut. No pressing since 15 November: smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8 that night, shoulder press 50 for 9, 9, 9, 8 on 12 November. Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 15 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 10.6 a week done on average over the last four weeks (the fourth is this week, which so far holds only Pull A on 16 November and Legs A on 17 November).

side-delts.why: Raised on 18 November (version 14). Side delts decide how wide the shoulders look on stage and they had the smallest share of any scored muscle: 6 direct sets, 8 counted, against 15.5 counted for rear delts. Lateral raises go to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted with the half credit from the shoulder press, the bottom of the new 10 to 20 range. The lift is moving: 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 logged live on 15 November, up from 15 for 15, 15, 12 on 4 November (the 12 November numbers were typed seconds apart from memory, so they are not counted here). It stays on two days, the push days. On the same count rear delts are at 12.5, so side delts are still behind them and sit on the floor of their range. A third lateral day would undo the 14 November change four days later with no night logged at four sets, so the next step waits for evidence: after the four-set nights on 19 and 22 November, the review of 24 November decides (the first likely to hold the 22 November log, since logs reach the repo a day or more late) between a third lateral day and a second side-delt lift. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 10 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 7 a week done on average over the last four weeks (the fourth is this week, which so far holds only Pull A on 16 November and Legs A on 17 November).

rear-delts.why: Cut on 18 November (version 14). Rear delts had 10 direct sets and 15.5 counted, nearly double the side delts, and they get help from every row and pulldown. The reverse pec deck comes off Push A and stays on Push B: 7 direct sets (reverse pec deck 3, face pulls 2 on each pull day), 12.5 counted, inside the new 6 to 14. Face pulls stay at two sets on both pull days, the count you asked for on 28 August. Reverse pec deck 97.5 for 12, 12, 12 on 12 and 15 November; face pulls 32.5 for 12, 12 on 16 November. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 12.5 planned a week, of which 7 are direct sets; 10.9 a week done on average over the last four weeks (the fourth is this week, which so far holds only Pull A on 16 November and Legs A on 17 November).

neck.why: Raised today from nothing. You wrote on 18 November that the program had no neck work and that this is an obvious miss in bodybuilding training; you were right, and neck was not even one of the muscles the reviews counted. Today neck gets a range of 4 to 12 counted sets a week and two lifts that need only a flat bench and a plate, since you have no harness and no neck machine: lying plate neck flexion, two sets last on Push A (first on 22 November), and lying plate neck extension, two sets straight after the shrugs on Pull B (first on 20 November). That is 4 direct sets a week, the bottom of the range, because no neck training appears anywhere in the log and a neck is brought up light and for reps. Both start with a 10 lb plate for 15 to 20 reps. Once both lifts have run twice with all reps done and no neck pain, the next step is a second set day for each, toward 8 a week. Nothing has been done yet, so the four-week average is 0.

prep.plan: Three weeks come before prep. This week (to 24 November) is the last build week, with the numbers on the cards. The week of 25 November is the lighter week: the calendar sets it at about 60 percent of the usual sets with weights about 20 percent lighter, and nothing taken near failure. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (24 November review) and your answer on calves; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 21 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (22 February to 1 March): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the three weeks before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters this week and not in December.

changes_today.why: You wrote on 18 November that there were no neck exercises in the program and that this is an obvious miss in bodybuilding training. You were right: neck was not one of the muscles the program counted, so no review could see it. The neck now has a weekly range of 4 to 12 counted sets. The neck is seen in every front and back pose and frames the traps, but it is a small muscle that has never been trained in this log, so it starts at the bottom of that range and climbs once it has shown it recovers. Every other range is unchanged.

Neck flexion trains the front of the neck, the part the front poses show. It needs only a flat bench and a plate, both at your gym; you said on 18 November you have no harness and no neck machine, so it is built around those. It goes last on Push A, which at 17 sets and 49 minutes on 15 November is the shortest day of the week, so Push A becomes 19 sets. Two sets of 15 to 20 with a light plate: necks are trained light and for reps, and this is the first neck work in the log.

Neck extension trains the back of the neck, which shows with the traps in the back poses. It goes straight after the shrugs on Pull B, so the upper traps and neck are trained together, on a flat bench with a plate. Pull B becomes 22 sets; on 13 November it ran 20 of its then 21 sets in 53 minutes, with the shrug's fourth set missing; that set is the one on watch, and if it goes missing again the shrug drops to three sets and Pull B to 21. Two sets of 15 to 20 with a light plate.
